name: Linux Terminal Navigation
whyWeUseIt: Terminal navigation commands allow you to move between directories, inspect files, and manage projects directly from the command line without needing a graphical interface. We use them together to explore the filesystem, check where we are, and manage files quickly.

commands.notes: Print Working Directory: tells you your exact full path in the filesystem

commands.whatItDoes: List all files and hidden files with permissions and size details
Move up one directory level to the parent folder
commands.notes: Two dots (..) represent the parent directory

commands.whatItDoes: Create a new empty file named index.html
commands.notes: Also updates the file timestamp if it already exists

name: Git Workflow Fundamentals
whyWeUseIt: Git is the industry standard for tracking code changes, collaborating with teammates, and reverting bugs. We use these core commands consecutively in our daily development loop to stage, commit, and sync code to remote repositories.

commands.whatItDoes: Check current branch, modified files, and staged changes
commands.notes: Run this frequently to see the state of your working tree

commands.whatItDoes: Stage all current modified and newly created files
commands.notes: Prepares changes to be captured in the next commit snapshot

commands.whatItDoes: Commit staged changes with a descriptive message
commands.notes: Saves your snapshot permanently to local Git history

commands.whatItDoes: Upload local commits to the remote main branch
commands.notes: Syncs your work with GitHub / GitLab
